about: Catalogue v1 of the modes the classifier decodes or will classify: the amateur and maritime/aeronautical modes with public specifications, and the military and government modems of docs/RESEARCH.md section 3 with the parameters the program can measure (their sync patterns are still only in docs/RESEARCH.md; frame periods are in 'frame_ms'). JSON, which is also valid YAML 1.2. Each parameter carries its provenance: 'documented' = from the cited specification, 'observed' = measured on recordings by someone, cited; 'guess' = not established. The 'match' blocks are read by the program (core/src/catalogue.cpp): the measured features of an emission no decoder recognised are compared with them, and the modes they are consistent with are listed. That is not an identification: many modes share parameters. 'in_program' says what the program does with the mode today and how that was tested. Provenance of 'match' parameters: 'documented' (the specification), 'vendor' (a decoder vendor's documentation, e.g. Wavecom), 'observed' (analysts, e.g. sigidwiki), 'measured' (in this project, on recordings supplied for it), 'guess'. A block's 'frame_provenance' and 'frame_source', when given, are those of its 'frame_ms'.

sources.QEX2020: S. Franke, B. Somerville, J. Taylor, 'The FT4 and FT8 Communication Protocols', QEX July/August 2020
sources.WSJTX: WSJT-X User Guide (J. Taylor et al.), wsjt.sourceforge.io
sources.WSPR: J. Taylor, 'WSPR' protocol description in the WSJT-X User Guide and K1JT's WSPR documentation
sources.G3PLX: P. Martinez, G3PLX, 'PSK31: a new radio-teletype mode', RadCom Dec 1998/Jan 1999
sources.FLDIGI: fldigi (W1HKJ et al.) source code, src/psk/psk.cxx: symbol lengths at 8000 samples/s (256, 128, 64, 32, 16 for 31.25 to 500 Bd, BPSK and QPSK alike), QPSK's convolutional code (constraint length 5, polynomials 0x17 and 0x19) and the preamble and postamble; read as a reference, no code copied
sources.M476: ITU-R M.476 and M.625 (direct-printing telegraph equipment, SITOR); ITU-R M.540 (NAVTEX)
sources.OLIVIA: P. Jalocha, SP9VRC, Olivia MFSK description; fldigi documentation
sources.MFSK: M. Greenman, ZL1BPU, MFSK16 description; fldigi documentation
sources.MIL141: MIL-STD-188-141B/D (ALE 2G appendix A, 3G appendix C, 4G appendix G); FED-STD-1045
sources.VARA: VARA HF documentation (J. A. Ruiz, EA5HVK); a proprietary modem
sources.SSTV: Dayton Paper (J. Langner, 'Proposal for SSTV Mode Specifications', 1998)
sources.WAVECOM: Wavecom decoder online help, mode pages (docs/RESEARCH.md source [11]); a decoder vendor's documentation, not the originators'
sources.SIGIDWIKI: Signal Identification Wiki, raw pages for each mode (docs/RESEARCH.md source [12]); analysts' observations
sources.I56578: i56578-swl blog posts on Akula and CIS Navy FSK (docs/RESEARCH.md sources [15], [35], [36], [37])
sources.I56578-SCRAMBLER: i56578-swl blog, 'STANAG 5511 Link-11 SLEW scrambler' (13 May 2016), quoting MIL-STD-188-110A: the data scrambler is reset after every 160 transmit symbols (docs/RESEARCH.md source [42])
sources.RIVET: Rivet source code, CIS3650.java (docs/RESEARCH.md source [38]); a hobbyist decoder
sources.USER-SA: Signals Analyzer screenshots supplied for the project (docs/RESEARCH.md source [39])
sources.RESEARCH-3.6: Measured in this project on recordings supplied for it (docs/RESEARCH.md section 3.6)

modes.name: FT8
modes.modulation: 8-GFSK (BT 2.0)

timing.value: 15 s UTC slots, 79 symbols = 12.64 s, starting 0.5 s into the slot

dial_frequencies_khz.note: WSJT-X defaults as commonly listed; not checked against the WSJT-X source

modes.in_program: decoded (ft8_lib) in the sub-band at each dial frequency inside the receiver's band; tested on synthetic signals only

modes.name: FT4
modes.modulation: 4-GFSK (BT 1.0)

dial_frequencies_khz.note: WSJT-X defaults as commonly listed; not checked against the WSJT-X source

modes.in_program: decoded (ft8_lib) like FT8; tested on synthetic signals only

modes.name: WSPR
modes.modulation: 4-FSK

timing.value: 2-minute slots starting on even minutes, 162 symbols = 110.6 s

modes.in_program: decoded (core/src/wspr.cpp) per 2-minute slot in the sub-band at each dial frequency inside the receiver's band: standard messages (callsign, 4-character locator, power) that pass every check and agree with 75 % of the received tones. Down to about -25 dB SNR in 2500 Hz on synthetic slots; both of the Signal Identification Wiki's recordings decode

modes.name: JS8
modes.modulation: 8-GFSK, the FT8 waveform with other framing

baud.note: 'normal' speed; faster and slower submodes exist with other parameters

modes.in_program: not decoded: JS8 differs from FT8 in its sync arrays and message packing (JS8 documentation), so the FT8 decoder is not expected to decode it (not tested); not classified yet

modes.name: PSK31
modes.modulation: BPSK, raised-cosine shaped, differential; Varicode

bandwidth_hz.note: the necessary bandwidth commonly given for PSK31 (emission designator 60H0J2B); not from G3PLX's article, which gives the baud rate

modes.in_program: decoded (PSK decoder from sdr_plugin_psk) on emissions up to 250 Hz wide, or measured at 31.25 Bd, when the text reads like radio traffic; tested on synthetic signals and the sigidwiki's example recording

modes.name: PSK63
modes.modulation: BPSK as PSK31, twice the rate

baud.note: the rate as fldigi implements it; G3PLX's article gives PSK31's 31.25 Bd

modes.in_program: decoded (same decoder) on emissions up to 250 Hz wide, or measured at 62.5 Bd; tested on synthetic signals and the sigidwiki's example recording

modes.name: PSK125
modes.modulation: BPSK as PSK31, four times the rate

baud.note: the rate as fldigi implements it

modes.in_program: decoded (same decoder) on emissions 100-250 Hz wide, or measured at 125 Bd; tested on synthetic signals and the sigidwiki's example recording

modes.name: PSK250
modes.modulation: BPSK as PSK31, eight times the rate
modes.in_program: decoded (same decoder) on emissions 250-800 Hz wide, or measured at 250 Bd; tested on synthetic signals and the sigidwiki's example recording

modes.name: PSK500
modes.modulation: BPSK as PSK31, sixteen times the rate
modes.in_program: decoded (same decoder) on emissions 500-1250 Hz wide, or measured at 500 Bd; tested on synthetic signals and the sigidwiki's example recording

modes.name: QPSK31
modes.modulation: differential QPSK, raised-cosine shaped; each Varicode bit through a rate 1/2, constraint length 5 convolutional code (polynomials 0x17, 0x19) as one of four phase changes
modes.in_program: decoded (same decoder: soft-decision Viterbi, either sense of rotation) alongside PSK31; tested on synthetic signals and the sigidwiki's example recording. Shares every measured parameter with PSK31: the decoders tell them apart

modes.name: QPSK63
modes.modulation: QPSK31 at twice the rate
modes.in_program: decoded (same decoder) alongside PSK63; tested on synthetic signals and the sigidwiki's example recording

modes.name: QPSK125
modes.modulation: QPSK31 at four times the rate
modes.in_program: decoded (same decoder) alongside PSK125; tested on synthetic signals and the sigidwiki's example recording

modes.name: QPSK250
modes.modulation: QPSK31 at eight times the rate
modes.in_program: decoded (same decoder) alongside PSK250; tested on synthetic signals and the sigidwiki's example recording

modes.name: QPSK500
modes.modulation: QPSK31 at sixteen times the rate
modes.in_program: decoded (same decoder) alongside PSK500; tested on synthetic signals and the sigidwiki's example recording

modes.name: RTTY 45.45/170
modes.modulation: 2-FSK, ITA2 start/stop (1 start, 5 data, 1.5 stop bits)

baud.note: the amateur convention (60 words per minute); ITU-T S.1 defines the code, not this speed

shift_hz.note: the amateur convention, not from ITU-T S.1

modes.in_program: decoded (FSK decoder from sdr_plugin_navtex) on emissions 200-700 Hz wide when the text reads like radio traffic; tested on synthetic signals only

modes.name: RTTY 50/450
modes.modulation: 2-FSK, ITA2 start/stop

baud.note: as listed for the German Weather Service's RTTY broadcasts by monitoring sites; not checked against the service's own schedule here

modes.in_program: decoded (same decoder) on emissions 350-900 Hz wide when the text reads like radio or weather traffic; tested on synthetic signals only. Its two tones start together, so they are one emission

modes.name: CW
modes.modulation: on-off keyed carrier

speed.value: any; the decoder follows the speed

modes.in_program: decoded (Morse decoder from sdr_plugin_ook) on emissions up to 250 Hz wide (occupied bandwidth) when the text reads like radio traffic or code groups; tested on synthetic signals only. The first letter or so is lost while the emission is confirmed

modes.name: NAVTEX / SITOR-B
modes.modulation: 2-FSK, CCIR 476 7-bit code with time-diversity FEC (mode B)

frequencies_khz.note: NAVTEX; SITOR-B is also used elsewhere

modes.in_program: decoded (NAVTEX decoder from sdr_plugin_navtex, with the ZCZC/NNNN message layer) on emissions 200-700 Hz wide; tested on synthetic signals only

modes.name: ALE 2G
modes.modulation: 8-FSK, 125 Bd, tones 750-2500 Hz in 250 Hz steps; Golay(24,12) and triple redundancy
modes.in_program: decoded (ALE decoder from sdr_plugin_navtex) on emissions 1300-3600 Hz wide; tested on synthetic signals only, down to about 0 dB SNR in 2.5 kHz

modes.name: ALE 3G / 4G (WALE)
modes.modulation: 8-PSK burst waveforms at 2400 symbols/s on an 1800 Hz carrier
modes.in_program: decoded (same decoder) on emissions 1300-3600 Hz wide; tested end to end on synthetic signals, and on the sigidwiki's real samples, whose three bursts arrive intact but protected (linking protection: their CRCs fail) and are reported as such

modes.name: Olivia
modes.modulation: MFSK; submodes named tones/bandwidth (e.g. 8/250, 8/500, 16/500, 32/1000); baud = bandwidth / tones
modes.provenance_note: parameters by submode, documented in OLIVIA

modes.name: Contestia
modes.modulation: MFSK derived from Olivia, with shorter symbols blocks and 6-bit characters

modes.name: MFSK16
modes.modulation: 16-tone MFSK

modes.name: MFSK32
modes.modulation: 16-tone MFSK, twice MFSK16's rate

modes.name: Feld Hell
modes.modulation: on-off keyed pixels, 122.5 pixels/s

modes.name: Radiofax (WEFAX)
modes.modulation: frequency-modulated subcarrier: black 1500 Hz, white 2300 Hz in a USB receiver tuned 1.9 kHz below the assigned frequency (+-400 Hz; +-150 Hz on long wave); 120 lines a minute (60, 90, 240 exist), index of cooperation 576 or 288; start tone 300 Hz (IOC 576) or 675 Hz (IOC 288), stop tone 450 Hz
modes.in_program: decoded (core/src/fax.cpp): recognised from 20 s of lines repeating at one of the line rates; the picture is saved as a PNG, straightened, and aligned when phasing lines were received. Tested on synthetic charts and on the Signal Identification Wiki's recordings: its four samples longer than 25 s give their pictures
modes.provenance_note: documented: the WMO facsimile standard (WMO-No. 386) as given in NOAA's Worldwide Marine Radiofacsimile Broadcast Schedules

modes.name: Time signal
modes.modulation: a carrier or tone marking every second (DCF77: carrier lowered 0.1/0.2 s; MSF: off 0.1-0.5 s; RBU, RWM, BPM, WWV, CHU, JJY, WWVB: pulses or ticks of their own)
modes.in_program: recognised by its seconds (core/src/timesig.cpp): the level repeats exactly every second for 12 s; the DCF77 and MSF time codes decoded, a minute reported only when every parity and fixed bit is right. The wiki's DCF77 and MSF recordings decode; 13 of its 20 recordings of ten stations are recognised
modes.provenance_note: documented: PTB's DCF77 time code and NPL's MSF time and date code

modes.name: SSTV
modes.modulation: analogue frequency-modulated subcarrier: 1200 Hz sync, 1500-2300 Hz image; VIS header at 1900/1200/1100/1300 Hz
modes.in_program: decoded (core/src/sstv.cpp): Martin M1/M2, Scottie S1/S2/DX, Robot 36/72 and PD 50 to 290, from the VIS header or (Martin, Scottie, PD) from the sync pulses' timing; the colour picture is saved as a PNG. Tested on synthetic pictures of every mode and on the Signal Identification Wiki's recordings: 9 of 14 give their pictures (the others: Robot 8, 12 and 24, one Robot recording without its header, one with the sidebands swapped)

modes.name: ARDOP
modes.modulation: 4-FSK, PSK and QAM frames in 200, 500, 1000 or 2000 Hz

modes.name: VARA HF
modes.modulation: OFDM-like multi-carrier; 2300 Hz standard, 500 Hz narrow
modes.provenance_note: bandwidths from VARA; the waveform is not published in detail

modes.name: DRM
modes.modulation: OFDM, robustness modes A-D, 4.5/5/9/10/18/20 kHz
modes.in_program: recognised (core/src/drm.cpp) by its OFDM guard interval, with its robustness mode; the programme is not decoded. Narrower than 3.2 kHz: labelled DRM-type OFDM (WinDRM, EasyPal, others may share the timing). 3 of the Signal Identification Wiki's 4 DRM recordings, its WinDRM one and both UK government WinDRM-type ones recognised

modes.name: SSB voice
modes.modulation: single sideband, suppressed carrier

modes.name: AM broadcast
modes.modulation: double sideband with carrier
modes.in_program: not classified yet; the carrier is detected as a narrow emission inside a wider one

modes.name: RTTY (other rates and shifts)
modes.modulation: 2-FSK, ITA2 start/stop at other rates and shifts

match.note: the wiki's RTTY page lists these shifts; its samples cover these rates

modes.in_program: decoded: RTTY decoders at the measured shift and rate (core/README.md); 17 of the wiki's 19 RTTY samples decode

modes.name: CIS-36-50 (T-600)
modes.modulation: 2-FSK, 5-bit characters as 7-bit constant-weight words

match.note: 50 Bd/1000 Hz before an Akula burst

modes.in_program: its 7-bit constant-weight code is recognised (core/src/constant_weight.cpp, labelled '4:3 code': other systems use such codes too), nothing decoded; found on 3 of the Signal Identification Wiki's 4 samples

modes.name: CIS-50-50
modes.modulation: 2-FSK; idle dot reversals at 50 Bd
modes.in_program: its 7-bit constant-weight code is recognised (core/src/constant_weight.cpp, labelled '4:3 code': other systems use such codes too), nothing decoded; found on the Signal Identification Wiki's sample

modes.name: CIS-12
modes.modulation: 12 DBPSK/DQPSK subcarriers 200 Hz apart, 120 Bd, pilot at +3300 Hz

modes.name: CIS BPSK 1200
modes.modulation: BPSK/SDPSK at 1200 Bd, about 2.5 kHz; a 512-bit block every 426.67 ms

modes.name: CIS MFSK-16 (XPA2)
modes.modulation: MFSK, 14 of 16 tone slots, 15 Hz apart, 7.5 Bd

modes.name: CIS-112
modes.modulation: OFDM, 112 DQPSK tones at 22.22 Bd; tone spacing not published

modes.name: CIS-3000
modes.modulation: 8PSK at 3000 Bd, about 3.4 kHz
modes.in_program: measured only (wider than the program's 2.6 kHz measuring channel)

modes.name: CIS-20
modes.modulation: OFDM, 20 DQPSK tones at 75 Bd, pilot at +3300 Hz, about 2.75 kHz

modes.name: CROWD36 (CIS-36 MFSK)
modes.modulation: MFSK, 36 tones 40 Hz apart

modes.name: Akula
modes.modulation: FSK bursts; also a BPSK burst (Akula II) and a 15-carrier DBPSK form
modes.in_program: recognised by its published sync and end groups (core/src/akula.cpp), not decoded; found on the recording of docs/RESEARCH.md section 3.6, where the groups were first checked

modes.name: Serdolik (command state)
modes.modulation: MFSK, 35 tones at 40 Bd; tone spacing not published

modes.name: STANAG 4285
modes.modulation: serial PSK at 2400 Bd on 1800 Hz; 106.67 ms frames

match.note: frame: 256 symbols, an 80-symbol preamble in every one

modes.name: STANAG 4529
modes.modulation: serial PSK at 1200 Bd; 213.33 ms frames; 1240 Hz

modes.name: STANAG 4539 / MIL-STD-188-110 App C
modes.modulation: serial PSK/QAM at 2400 Bd on 1800 Hz; 119.6 ms frames

match.note: frame: 256 data + 31 probe symbols. The probes are not the same in every frame, so the signal can repeat at a multiple of it instead (docs/RESEARCH.md section 3.7)

modes.name: MIL-STD-188-110 serial / STANAG 4415
modes.modulation: serial 8PSK at 2400 Bd on 1800 Hz; its probes repeat every 66.67 or 200 ms

match.note: frame: the scrambler restarts every 160 symbols (I56578-SCRAMBLER, quoting the standard), so the known probe symbols repeat every 160 symbols (66.67 ms) with 20 data / 20 probe frames (up to 1200 bps, and 110A-MOD) and every 480 (200 ms) with 32/16 frames (2400 and 4800 bps); the preamble is built of 200 ms segments (WAVECOM). Both periods measured on the wiki's samples (docs/RESEARCH.md section 3.7)

modes.name: MIL-STD-188-110 App A (16-tone)
modes.modulation: 16 tones, 75 Bd DQPSK/BPSK, Doppler pilot at 605 Hz

modes.name: MIL-STD-188-110 App B (39-tone) / STANAG 4197
modes.modulation: 39 tones at 44.44 Bd

modes.name: HFDL
modes.modulation: burst PSK at 1800 Bd on a 1440 Hz subcarrier
modes.in_program: decoded (core/src/hfdl.cpp): PDUs whose frame check is right, all the time on channels a frequency list names, else on emissions 1800-3600 Hz wide. Tested on synthetic bursts of every mode and on the five recordings of the Signal Identification Wiki (19 of their 21 bursts; no 8PSK among them)

modes.name: Link-11 CLEW
modes.modulation: 16 DQPSK tones 110 Hz apart (935-2365 Hz plus 2915 Hz), Doppler tone 605 Hz

modes.name: Link-11 SLEW
modes.modulation: serial PSK at 2400 Bd on 1800 Hz (QPSK per Wavecom, 8PSK per sigidwiki)

modes.name: CODAN Selcal
modes.modulation: FSK 100 Bd, mark 1870 / space 1700 Hz, ITU-R M.493 alphabet

modes.name: CODAN 3212
modes.modulation: serial PSK/QAM at 1800 Bd centred on 1500 Hz

modes.name: CODAN chirp (ALE)
modes.modulation: 32 DBPSK carriers 80 Hz apart at 80 Bd, 2560 Hz

modes.name: CODAN 9001
modes.modulation: 16 DQPSK tones 112.5 Hz apart at 75 Bd

modes.name: DSC-HF
modes.modulation: FSK 100 Bd, 170 Hz, 10-bit symbols (ITU-R M.493)
modes.in_program: decoded (core/src/dsc.cpp): calls whose error-check character is right. Tested on synthetic calls and on the four HF recordings of the Signal Identification Wiki

modes.name: SITOR-A
modes.modulation: FSK ARQ, 100 Bd, 450 ms cycle

modes.name: PACTOR I
modes.modulation: FSK ARQ, 200 Hz shift, 1.25 s cycle

modes.name: PACTOR II
modes.modulation: two DPSK channels at 100 Bd, about 450-500 Hz

modes.name: PACTOR III
modes.modulation: 2-18 DBPSK/DQPSK tones 120 Hz apart at 100 Bd

modes.name: Polish F11
modes.modulation: FSK 100 Bd, 625 Hz

modes.name: Chinese 4+4
modes.modulation: 8 DQPSK tones at 75 Bd, 300/450 Hz apart
